title: Sentinel weight gateway and compatibility checker
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Build a hardened gateway service (Sentinel) that centralizes open-LLM weight intake, performs deterministic conversion steps, runs a layered compatibility checker, and publishes a pinned runtime artifact + performance profile. The goal is a dependable end-to-end flow from raw weight bundle to a runtime-ready pinned model that includes reproducible smoke results and telemetry for release decisions. This ticket scopes the core Sentinel components, the canary verification harness, failure modes, and the minimal UX hooks required by Console for rollout metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel accepts weight bundles in tar/zip and S3/HTTP manifests and records provenance metadata
Automated conversion produces runtime-compatible artifacts for CPU/GPU variants with deterministic checksums
Compatibility checker validates layer shapes, dtype/quantization candidates, and KV cache readiness with defined pass/fail signals
Canary smoke suite executes 3 prompt families (generation, chat, long-context KV reuse) and publishes latency/quality metrics to Console
Pin publishing API writes model pin and performance profile to the canonical catalog with rollback metadata
Telemetry captures conversion warnings, checksum diffs, and canary regressions; alerts for high-severity failures
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Ingest API + provenance capture (S3/http/manifest support)
Phase 2: Conversion pipeline: weight format normalizer -> dtype/shape validation -> compiled artifact builder
Phase 3: Compatibility checker: shape contracts, kv-cache smoke, quantization-scan (no destructive quantization)
Phase 4: Canary harness: three curated prompt sets, deterministic RNG seeds, token-level latency traces
Phase 5: Pin & profile publisher: create pin object, attach performance JSON, sign with release key
Phase 6: Integrations: Console metadata hooks, PRD link, and runtime rollout policy support
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Heterogeneous checkpoints with nonstandard naming may map incorrectly -> Mitigation: layered file fingerprinting and a human-review fallback route
Risk: Conversion nondeterminism on quantization paths -> Mitigation: deterministic seed paths, golden-run smoke against reference VM
Risk: Canary flakiness causing false negatives -> Mitigation: statistical pass thresholds and repeated runs; store raw traces for debug
Risk: Secret/PII in community weights -> Mitigation: manifest scanning + take-down escalation policy and security review gate
timeline: Week 1 (Mar 5-11): API + provenance prototype; initial S3 manifest parser
Week 2 (Mar 12-18): Conversion pipeline POC and checksum validation; integrate shape checker
Week 3 (Mar 19-25): Canary harness and curated prompt packs; basic Console telemetry plumbing
Week 4 (Mar 26-Apr 1): End-to-end run, pin publish test, and security review; prepare launch PR
checklist: Define manifest schema and required provenance fields
Implement non-blocking linting for weight contents
Add deterministic conversion runner with reproducible outputs
Ship canary prompt sets and deterministic seeds
Publish performance profile schema to catalog service
Add Console hooks for pin metadata and canary status
progress_updates: 2026-03-06: Prototype ingestion API finished; captured provenance fields: source_url, sha256, declared_license
2026-03-08: Conversion runner can normalize HF-style checkpoints to runtime artifact for small model sample; checksum deterministic across runs on same HW
2026-03-09: First iteration of shape checker flagged subtle dimension mismatches for nested adapter layouts; created mapping heuristics
2026-03-11: Canary harness integrated three prompt families and baseline traces are generated; observed unexpected latency spike during KV expansion on sequence length 32->2048
2026-03-12: Investigation ongoing for KV latency spike; mitigation: cap initial canary sequences and add memory layout probes. Security review request filed (sec-REQ-447).
notes: This ticket aims to reduce manual steps in community model onboarding and minimize incidents caused by bad pins. The Sentinel name is intentionally used to denote a small safety/compatibility guard before models are published. We will keep destructive operations (quantization) behind an explicit 'opt-in' flag in this iteration.
postmortem_hook: If a pin causes a production regression, attach incident link and remedial steps here for rapid rollback
